key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger dramatically boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical route to improve CO2 conversion systems by combining catalyst surface/charge engineering with a carbon-negative biological co-feed.
method: Designed an AB2O6 high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to increase CO2 adsorption, Bi to promote polarization and charge separation, and Nb/Ta to support charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO only, with microplastics, and with microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining stable microalgae–catalyst coupling and requires assessment of long-term scalability, light utilization, and product separation.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
